tip.title: Practice the phrases you will actually use on the ship
tip.body: Tonight's Spanish session is a good chance to drill the handful of lines you will use in port, like asking for the check, asking prices, and asking where something is. Saying them out loud a few times builds recall much faster than reading them, and it makes the cruise days feel easier.

ottoman.chapterTitle: Chapter 14: The end of the caliphate
ottoman.summary: When the sultanate was abolished in November 1922, the Ankara assembly kept a separate caliphate and named Abdülmecid II caliph without making him sultan. That arrangement proved unstable, and on 3 March 1924 the Turkish assembly abolished the caliphate and expelled the Ottoman dynasty. The decision grounded the new republic's sovereignty in national institutions while leaving a wider argument about religious authority, from British India's Khilafat movement onward, unresolved.

surprise.title: La cuenta, por favor
surprise.body: Tonight's Spanish block lands twelve days before Carnival Paradise, and this is the line that brings the check when dinner wraps in a Spanish-speaking port. La cuenta means the bill, por favor keeps it polite, and together they work at cafés and restaurants from Tampa out through the Caribbean. Tap play to hear cuenta in native Spanish, then say the full phrase out loud twice before you close the books.
